Note::narrow¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::narrow(std::int64_t dim, std::int64_t start, std::int64_t length) const

Keep A Contiguous Slice Along One Axis¶

narrow(dim, start, length) returns a Note that keeps only positions [start, start + length) along axis dim, with every other axis untouched. The rank does not change — narrowing a 2 × 3 grid to length 2 columns gives a 2 × 2 grid. Use it to take the first n rows, a window of columns, or a middle span, without collapsing the axis the way select does.

Nothing about the text changes: the kept cells are shared with the source, the bytes-vs-UTF-8 mode carries over, and the cost is one O(result numel) copy of the offset table.

The arguments¶

Argument

Meaning

dim

Which axis to slice. 0 is the outermost; a negative value counts from the back (-1 is the last axis). After that adjustment it must be in [0, dim()), otherwise dim out of range.

start

The first position to keep along dim. Must be in [0, size(dim)] — non-negative, and size(dim) itself is allowed (paired only with length 0). Otherwise narrow start out of range.

length

How many positions to keep. Must be ≥ 0 (narrow length must be non-negative), and start + length must not exceed size(dim) (narrow range out of bounds).

length 0 is valid and yields an empty Note (that axis becomes size 0). start 0 with length equal to size(dim) returns the Note unchanged. There is no negative start and no step; for scattered or reordered positions use take.

Example 1: A Window Of A 1-D Note¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.narrow(0, 1, 3)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["b", "c", "d"]

Positions 1, 2, 3 — start is inclusive, start + length is exclusive.

Example 2: Rows Versus Columns Of A Grid¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.narrow(0, 1, 1)) << "\n";   // one row, axis kept
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.narrow(1, 0, 2)) << "\n";   // first two columns

Output¶

Note(shape=[1, 3], dim=2, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["d", "e", "f"]
]
Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a", "b"], 
  ["d", "e"]
]

narrow(0, 1, 1) keeps row 1 but stays rank 2 (1 × 3), unlike select(0, 1) which would give a rank-1 [3].

Example 3: Negative dim¶

const auto m = pluss::make_note({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(m.narrow(-1, 1, 2)) << "\n";   // last axis, columns 1..2

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["b", "c"], 
  ["e", "f"]
]

Example 4: Zero Length And Full Range¶

const auto v = pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.narrow(0, 2, 0)) << "\n";   // empty
std::cout << pluss::note::print(v.narrow(0, 0, 6)) << "\n";   // unchanged

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"]

Example 5: Rejections¶

auto first_line = [](const pluss::Error& e) {
  const std::string m = e.what();
  return m.substr(0, m.find('\n'));
};

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c"}).narrow(0, 2, 2); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

try { (void)pluss::make_note({"a", "b", "c"}).narrow(0, -1, 1); }
catch (const pluss::Error& e) { std::cout << first_line(e) << "\n"; }

Output¶

narrow range out of bounds
narrow start out of range

start + length = 4 exceeds the axis size 3; and start may not be negative.

See Also¶

  • Note::select: pick one slab along an axis and drop the axis.

  • Note::take: gather arbitrary, possibly repeated or reordered positions.

  • Note::split: cut each cell’s text into pieces (a different kind of slicing).
